observations: The bind-pose hero and side views read as one original articulated jungle viper: a long tapered body, bright bramble thorns, alternating gold scale bands, and a broad paired rainleaf hood create a clear silhouette from tail to skull.

The portrait view keeps two pale luminous eyes, ivory jaw detail, hood panels, a central crown thorn, cheek thorns, and the orchid tongue visually distinct from the body; these are authored geometry tied to native head, jaw, tongue, and joint13 palette entries.

Every visible surface in the rendered scenes comes from the original source GLB and its palette texture. The studio scenes contain no native body surface, native fall-off piece, native camera, native material, or game texture.
limits: This is a static offline bind-pose review under studio lighting, not an FTK combat camera, native material, animation, portrait, culling, ragdoll, lifecycle, or gameplay result.
The separate BackRib, FrontRib, head, jaw, and seven-bone tongue construction needs native idle, bite, venom, hit, DeathLight, and ordinary Death review before animation-safe or finished-art claims.

Jungle C normal Death is source-proven to hide enJungleSnakeC and activate 13 native quetzalPiece fall-off fragments. This review does not accept their visual relationship to Bramblecoil or claim a normal-death custom-body result.
decision: The source is readable and materially distinct enough to justify one fresh exact snakeJungleC/enJungleSnakeC isolated binding trial. The normal-death fall-off path stays a separately recorded integration boundary.
